description: a wildfire sensor sends a smoke alert to the dispatch center, which checks it against satellite images. if the satellite confirms a fire dispatch pages the duty ranger, otherwise it logs a false alarm and keeps watching the sensor. the ranger drives out and estimates the spread, and unless the wind is above forty kilometres an hour the ranger sends a ground crew. when the wind is too strong the ranger calls the regional command, which orders an evacuation through the county sheriff. the sheriff texts every resident in the zone, and residents who don't reply within ten minutes get a door knock from a deputy. once the crew contains the fire they report back to dispatch, which closes the incident.

errors.detail: After logging a false alarm, dispatch keeps watching the sensor, but False Alarm has no edge back to Wildfire Sensor.
The 'Wind above 40 km/h?' decision has only a 'no' edge. Its 'yes' outcome, where the ranger calls regional command, is missing.

'Wind too strong?' duplicates the wind decision and is checked by Ground Crew. The ranger makes that decision, and the evacuation path should branch from the ranger's wind check, not follow the crew being sent.
Dispatch never closes the incident. 'Fire Reported?' leads back to Dispatch Center, and no closing step follows.
The ranger driving out and estimating the spread is not shown as a step before the wind decision.
The ten-minute no-reply condition is only a vague 'missed reply' label, not a decision. The deputy's door knock is also not tied to the unresponsive residents.

description: the transplant coordinator gets a donor kidney and runs it through the matching system. the matching system ranks waiting patients by blood type and tissue match and sends the top patient to the surgeon. if the surgeon accepts the organ the hospital calls the patient in, otherwise the matching system offers it to the next patient on the list. when the patient arrives the lab cross-matches their blood again and only if the cross-match is negative does the surgery go ahead, else the kidney goes back to the matching system. after surgery the recovery ward monitors the patient and pages the surgeon if creatinine rises.

errors.detail: The Hospital box (calls the patient in when the surgeon accepts) has no outgoing edge, so the accept path dead-ends. The Lab cross-match is instead reached only through Next Patient, the rejection path, so a patient accepted on the first offer never reaches the Lab.
The 'Pages Surgeon' box is not connected to the Surgeon box, so the page never reaches the surgeon and the flow dead-ends.

description: telemetry from the satellite comes down through a ground station, and there is a decoder in front of the mission database. the decoder checks every frame's checksum and drops it if the checksum fails, otherwise it writes the frame to the mission database. an anomaly detector reads the database every minute and if a reading is out of range it alerts the flight controller. the flight controller decides whether it's a real fault; if it is they upload a safe-mode command back to the satellite through the ground station, if it isn't they mark the alert as noise. the database is replicated and uses round robin.

errors.detail: The checksum-passes path is missing: there is no 'no' edge from 'Checksum failed?' to the mission database, where the frame should be written. Only an unlabeled-condition 'routes to' edge from Decoder to the database exists.
The 'Frame Log' box is invented. The text says a frame that fails the checksum is dropped, not logged.
'Real fault?' with 'no' points to Satellite. The text says the flight controller marks the alert as noise, so it should go to 'Alert Noise', which is left orphaned.
'Real fault?' with 'yes' goes directly to Ground Station instead of to the Safe-Mode Command upload. The command then reaches the satellite only via a roundabout Ground Station edge.

description: a customer files a car insurance claim in the app, and the app sends it to the claims service. the claims service runs a fraud model on it. claims the model scores as high risk go to the special investigations unit, the rest go to an adjuster. the adjuster asks the customer for photos and if the photos are missing the adjuster chases the customer again. when the damage is under two thousand dollars the adjuster approves payment straight away, otherwise a senior adjuster has to sign off first. finance pays the approved claims and emails the customer a receipt. investigators who find fraud refer the claim to the police.

errors.detail: The 'Damage under two thousand?' yes branch loops back to Adjuster instead of leading to payment approval and on to Finance.
Senior Adjuster has no outgoing edge. The text says the senior adjuster signs off and the claim then goes to Finance for payment.
Special Investigations Unit is not connected to Investigators, so the high-risk path dead-ends before investigators examine the claim.
The edge Finance -> Claims Service 'pays claims' is not in the text. Finance pays the approved claims and no flow back to the claims service is described.
The adjuster asking the customer for photos is not drawn. The adjuster goes straight to a 'Photos missing?' check with no request edge to the Customer.
The Investigators -> Police referral has no 'fraud found?' decision, so the condition that investigators find fraud is not modeled.

description: the stage manager calls the cue on headset and the lighting operator presses go on the console. the console sends the cue over the network to the dimmer racks, and there is a network switch in front of the dimmer racks. if a dimmer rack doesn't acknowledge the cue the console retries it twice, and if it still fails the operator switches to the backup console. the follow spot operators also listen to the stage manager and pick up the lead actor when the stage manager says so. at the end of the act the stage manager tells the house manager, who opens the bar.

errors.detail: The console's two retries of the cue after a missing acknowledgement are absent; the decision goes straight to the backup console with no retry loop back to the console or dimmer racks.

The edge 'Stage Manager -> Lead Actor (says so)' is wrong; the follow spot operators pick up the lead actor when the stage manager says so, so the edge should go from Follow Spot Operators to Lead Actor.
The edge 'Cue on Headset -> Console (routes to)' is not described; the text only says the stage manager calls the cue and the operator presses go.

description: a beekeeper inspects each hive every week and records it in the hive log. if the beekeeper sees queen cells they split the colony into a new hive, otherwise they check the honey supers. supers that are more than eighty percent capped go to the extraction room, which spins them and sends the honey to the bottling line. the bottling line labels the jars only when the moisture reading is under eighteen percent; wetter honey goes back to the extraction room to dry. a distributor collects the labelled jars on fridays.

the passenger books a ferry ticket on the website, which asks the booking engine for a space on the sailing. the booking engine checks vehicle deck capacity and if the deck is full it puts the passenger on the waitlist, otherwise it holds a space and sends the passenger to payment. if the payment fails the booking engine releases the space. the waitlist service watches for cancellations and offers freed spaces to waitlisted passengers by sms. on the day the port gate scans the ticket and lets the car board unless the ticket is for a different sailing, in which case the gate sends the driver to the ticket office.

errors.detail: The 'unless' path is missing: when the ticket is for the right sailing, the gate lets the car board, but the diagram has no boarding box or edge.
The 'Different sailing?' decision is checked by the Ticket box, but the Port Gate is what makes that check.
The edge 'Ticket' -> 'Port Gate' labeled 'sends to' is not in the text and creates a loop between the gate and the ticket.
When payment fails, the 'yes' edge points back at the Space box. The text says the booking engine releases the space, so there should be a release step.
The edge 'Booking Engine' -> 'Sailing' duplicates the website's request. The text says the website asks the booking engine for a space on the sailing, not that the engine asks the sailing.

The waitlist service watches for cancellations, but the diagram has no cancellation step. It only shows the service watching the Waitlist and offering spaces to the Passenger, and it omits the SMS channel.

description: a clinic refers a patient to the clinical trial, and the research nurse screens them against the eligibility criteria. ineligible patients are referred back to the clinic. eligible patients sign a consent form, and the randomisation system assigns them to the drug arm or the placebo arm. the pharmacy dispenses the blinded kit for whichever arm they're in. every two weeks the nurse records side effects and if a side effect is serious the nurse reports it to the safety board within a day. the safety board can unblind the patient, and if the drug caused it the board stops the patient's treatment.

errors.detail: The 'Ineligible?' decision is fed by 'Clinical Trial', but the research nurse does the screening, so the nurse should be the one who checks it. The nurse's screening edge to 'Eligibility Criteria' never leads into the decision.
'Ineligible?' has no 'no' (eligible) path to 'Consent Form'. 'Consent Form' has no incoming edge, so the flow from screening to consent and randomisation is broken.
The diagram has no 'Drug caused it?' decision and no step where the board stops the patient's treatment. The flow ends at 'Unblinded Patient'.
The two-week recording interval and the one-day reporting deadline are not captured. The nurse's report to the safety board is also not labelled as the nurse's action.
The extra 'Referral' box and its 'routes to' edge back to 'Clinic' is a clumsy way to show sending the patient back. A direct 'refers back' edge from the 'yes' outcome to 'Clinic' would be correct.

description: trucks tip mixed recycling onto the intake belt, which carries it past a magnet that pulls out steel cans into the steel bay. the remaining material goes to an optical sorter which blows plastic bottles onto the plastics belt and lets paper fall through to the paper baler. a quality inspector watches the plastics belt and throws any paper back onto the intake belt. if the paper baler jams the line supervisor stops the intake belt until a mechanic clears it. full bales go to the loading dock where a buyer's truck collects them.

errors.detail: The remaining material after the magnet should go to the Optical Sorter, but the diagram routes it from Steel Bay, so the steel bay feeds the sorter and the Magnet has no onward path for the remaining material.

The mechanic clears the jam after the line supervisor stops the intake belt. The diagram instead sends the 'no' (no jam) outcome to Mechanic, and nothing connects the supervisor's stop to the mechanic's clearing.
Full bales go from the Paper Baler to the Loading Dock, but no edge connects them, so the Loading Dock has no incoming flow.
The buyer's truck collects bales from the loading dock, but the edge points from Loading Dock to Buyer's Truck labeled 'receives', which reverses the relation.

description: a player clicks find match and the client sends the request to the matchmaker. the matchmaker looks for players within one hundred rating points, and if it can't find nine others within thirty seconds it widens the range and searches again. once ten players are found the matchmaker asks the server allocator for a game server, and if no server is free in the player's region the allocator falls back to the nearest region. the game server loads the map and the clients connect to it. there's an anti-cheat service in front of the game server that kicks any client that fails its check. when the match ends the game server sends results to the rating service, which updates every player's rating.

errors.detail: The 'Within 100 points?' yes branch goes to 'Searches Again'. Finding enough players should move on to the ten-players/allocation step, and only the failed search should lead to widening and searching again.
'Widens Range' and 'Searches Again' dead-end. Nothing sends the matchmaker back to search again after the range is widened.
'Server free?' is checked by Anti-cheat (Anti-cheat -> Server free?). The allocator decides whether a server is free in the region, so Allocator should be the checker.
'Server free?' yes loops back to Anti-cheat instead of allocating the free game server, which then loads the map.
The fallback 'Region' box dead-ends. The allocator should use the nearest region to get a server, which then leads to the game server.
Client connects to 'Map' instead of to the game server. Because Anti-cheat sits in front of the server, the client should connect through Anti-cheat to the server.
There is no anti-cheat check decision with a pass/fail outcome. A client that fails should be kicked, and one that passes should be routed to the server.
The edge Anti-cheat -> Server labeled 'kicks client' misrepresents the flow. The anti-cheat should route passing clients to the server and kick only those that fail, not send them to the server.

description: the avalanche forecaster reads the overnight snow sensors every morning and rates the danger from one to five. when the rating is three or below the ski patrol opens the slopes as normal, the rest of the time the forecaster asks the patrol leader for a control mission. the patrol leader checks the weather and only if visibility is good does the helicopter fly the explosives team up, otherwise the mission waits an hour and the patrol leader checks again. after the blasts the team inspects each slope, and slopes that slid cleanly reopen while the others stay closed. the patrol leader reports every closure back to the forecaster.

errors.detail: When the rating is three or below, Ski Patrol is wired to Snow Sensors with 'routes to' instead of opening the slopes as normal.

The 'no' outcome of 'Slid cleanly?' loops back to Slopes, but the text says those slopes stay closed. There is no closed-slopes outcome, so the closures that the patrol leader reports are not tied to this path.
The extra edge from Patrol Leader to Avalanche Forecaster labeled 'routes to' is not in the text and duplicates the 'reports back to' edge.

description: a donor gives blood at the mobile clinic and the courier takes the bag to the blood bank. the lab tests every bag for infections and discards any bag that tests positive, the clean ones get separated into plasma and red cells. red cells go to the cold store and plasma goes to the freezer. when a hospital orders blood the dispatcher picks the oldest matching unit from the cold store, and on a miss it falls back to the regional blood bank. the dispatcher sends the unit by courier and the hospital confirms receipt.

errors.detail: The positive-test outcome is missing: no 'yes' edge from 'Positive?' to a discard step, so bags that test positive are never discarded.
The cold-store miss is not modeled. There is no decision box such as 'Unit in cold store?' and no regional blood bank box, so the fallback to the regional blood bank is absent.

The edge 'Dispatcher -> Unit (falls back to)' points to a generic 'Unit' box instead of the regional blood bank. The 'Cold Store -> Unit (matches)' edge is also invented and does not reflect the text.
The dispatcher sends the unit straight to the hospital. The text says it is sent by courier, so the courier leg is missing.
The receipt confirmation edge points to 'Confirms', which is not in the boxes list. The confirmation step is malformed and dead-ends rather than being a proper box.

description: each morning the vineyard manager samples grapes from every block and measures the sugar. blocks above twenty four brix get picked that day, the others are sampled again tomorrow. the pickers load the grapes into bins and a tractor hauls the bins to the crush pad. at the crush pad the sorting table removes leaves and rotten bunches, and the destemmer sends the clean fruit to the fermentation tanks. the winemaker tastes each tank daily and if fermentation stalls she adds yeast, else she leaves it until it's dry.

errors.detail: Blocks at or below 24 brix go to 'Sample Tomorrow', which dead-ends. The text says they are sampled again, so the flow should return to the sampling step.
The brix decision is fed by 'Block', but the decision rests on the sugar measurement made by the vineyard manager. It should come from 'Sugar' or 'Vineyard Manager'.
'Fermentation stalls?' is fed by 'Fermentation Tanks', but the winemaker tastes the tanks and makes that decision. The edge should come from 'Winemaker'.
The winemaker tastes each tank daily, but 'Yeast' has no outgoing edge and 'Dry' is not tied to the daily tasting. There is no loop back to re-check after adding yeast or while waiting for dryness.

description: the dentist scans the patient's tooth and uploads the scan to the dental lab portal. the portal queues it for a designer, who models the crown and sends the design back to the dentist for approval. if the dentist asks for changes the designer reworks it, otherwise the design goes to the milling machine. the milling machine cuts the crown from a zirconia block and the furnace sinters it. a technician checks the fit on a printed model and anything that doesn't fit goes back to the milling machine, the rest are shipped to the dentist.

errors.detail: The 'Changes needed?' decision is fed by the Designer, but the text says the dentist decides whether to ask for changes.
The 'Rework' box dead-ends. The designer's rework should loop back to the designer and then to the dentist for approval.
Nothing connects the Furnace to the Technician, so the sintered crown never reaches the fit check and the Technician has no incoming flow.
The edge 'Zirconia Block' to 'Furnace' (sinters) is wrong. The furnace sinters the cut crown from the milling machine, not the raw block, and the block is only the material.
The printed model the technician uses to check the fit is not shown.

description: a broadcaster uploads a film to the subtitling platform, which sends the audio to the speech recogniser. the recogniser produces a draft transcript and a translator corrects it and translates it. a reviewer watches the film with the subtitles and returns any scene with timing errors to the translator. once the reviewer signs off the platform burns the subtitles into a preview, and only when the broadcaster approves the preview does the platform deliver the final files. rejected previews go back to the reviewer.

errors.detail: The speech recogniser's draft transcript goes to the Reviewer, but the text says the translator corrects and translates it first.
Nothing leads from the Translator to the Reviewer, so the translator is a dead end and the reviewer never receives the translated subtitles to watch.
There is no decision box for the broadcaster's approval of the preview. Delivery of the final files is drawn as unconditional, and the send-back to the reviewer is not tied to a rejection.
There is no decision box for whether the reviewer finds timing errors. Returning scenes to the translator and signing off to the preview are both unconditional.

description: a reader emails the newspaper about a mistake and the email lands in the corrections inbox. the standards editor reads it and asks the reporter who wrote the story whether it's wrong. if the reporter agrees the standards editor writes a correction, if not the editor checks the source documents herself. corrections for print stories go to the night desk for tomorrow's paper, the rest are added to the web article straight away. the standards editor replies to the reader either way.

errors.detail: No edge from Corrections Inbox to Standards Editor, so the flow dead-ends at the inbox and never shows the standards editor reading the email.
The 'yes' outcome of 'Story wrong?' points back to Newspaper, but when the reporter agrees the standards editor writes a correction.
The 'no' outcome of 'Story wrong?' is missing; it should lead to the editor checking the source documents herself.

A separate 'Editor' box is invented, with 'Standards Editor writes correction' pointing to it. The text has the same standards editor writing the correction and checking the documents, and the writing step is not tied to the reporter's answer.

There is no 'Print story?' decision. Source Documents goes to both Night Desk and Web Article unconditionally, but the correction should go to the night desk only for print stories and to the web article otherwise. The correction, not the source check, should be what is routed.

The Reporter box leads into 'Story wrong?' with an empty label, but the text has the standards editor asking the reporter and the reporter answering. This is roughly right, but the decision is attributed oddly.

description: customers upload models to the print farm website and the slicer turns each model into print instructions. the scheduler sends jobs to the printers, there are twelve printers and the scheduler uses least connections. a camera watches every print and if it spots spaghetti it cancels the job and the scheduler requeues it. finished prints go to the post processing bench where a worker removes supports. prints that need painting go to the paint booth first, the others go straight to packing, and the courier collects from packing at five.

errors.detail: The edge between Slicer and Print Farm Website points from Slicer to the website, but the website's uploaded models should go to the Slicer.
There is no 'Needs painting?' decision after the post-processing bench. Printers go straight to Paint Booth, bypassing the bench, and the 'others go straight to packing' path is absent.
Paint Booth connects to Courier, but painted prints should go on to Packing.
The edge from Packing to Worker is not in the text. Packing is only collected by the courier.
'Printer (least connections)' is a redundant extra box alongside 'Printers (twelve)'. The replication strategy should be in a single printers box.
The spaghetti outcome never shows the job being cancelled before it is requeued. The 'no' path, where the print continues normally, is also absent.
The courier's collection at five is not captured.

description: the pilot requests pushback from ground control, which checks the departure queue. if the queue is longer than ten aircraft ground control holds the pilot at the gate, otherwise it clears the pushback. the pilot taxis to the runway holding point and switches to the tower. the tower clears the aircraft for takeoff unless another aircraft is on final approach, in which case the pilot waits and asks again. after takeoff the tower hands the aircraft to departure control.

errors.detail: The 'otherwise it clears the pushback' outcome is missing: the 'no' branch of 'Queue over ten?' loops back to Departure Queue instead of going to a pushback-clearance step, and nothing connects pushback clearance to the pilot taxiing.

description: each turbine streams vibration data to the monitoring centre, where a wear model scores it. turbines with a high score get a maintenance ticket, the others keep running. the planner looks at the ticket and the wind forecast, and crews only climb when the wind is below twelve metres per second, otherwise the planner reschedules the ticket for the next calm day. the crew replaces the worn part and records it in the asset system. if the turbine still vibrates after the restart the crew calls the manufacturer's engineer.

errors.detail: The 'Score high?' decision has no 'no' path, although the text says turbines with a lower score keep running.

The 'yes' outcome of the wind check goes to Wind Forecast, and Wind Forecast then feeds Crews with 'looks at'. The planner is the one who reads the forecast. When the wind is below twelve m/s, the crews should go straight to the climb and repair.
The 'no' outcome of the wind check sends the work to Crews. The text says the planner reschedules the ticket for the next calm day, so this should loop back to the ticket or planner.
The diagram has no box for replacing the worn part or restarting the turbine. Crews goes straight to recording and the vibration check.

description: a caller dials the emergency line and the call taker asks the triage questions. the triage software gives a priority, and priority one calls go straight to the nearest ambulance while lower priorities wait in the queue for a free crew. if no ambulance is free within eight minutes for a priority one call the dispatcher sends a fire engine as first responder. the crew treats the patient on scene and decides whether they need hospital. patients who don't are discharged at home, the others are taken to the emergency department, which the crew pre-alerts by radio.

errors.detail: There is no decision box such as 'Priority one?' fed by the triage software. Priority One and Priority Two are plain boxes, and Priority Two has no incoming edge from triage.
Priority One → Waiting Queue 'waits' is invented. Priority one calls go straight to the ambulance, and only lower priorities wait in the queue.
Waiting Queue dead-ends. Lower-priority calls should leave it when a crew becomes free and an ambulance is sent.
The 'Ambulance free?' outcome is inverted. Dispatching a fire engine should follow 'no' (no ambulance free within eight minutes), but the diagram draws it as 'yes'.
'Ambulance free?' has no outcome where an ambulance is available. Ambulance never leads to On Scene, so only the fire engine route reaches treatment.

The hospital decision is checked by a made-up 'Hospital' box. It should be made by the crew on scene ('Needs hospital?'). The diagram turns the decision into an On Scene → Hospital step and then a vague 'Patient stable?' check.
The pre-alert edge points from Emergency Dept to Radio Crew. The crew should pre-alert the emergency department by radio.
The call taker and the triage software are not modelled as separate actors. The emergency line asks the triage questions directly, and nothing gives the priority.

description: parents apply online and the council's admissions system checks the home address. children inside the catchment get a place offer from the school, everyone else goes on the waiting list ranked by distance. parents have two weeks to accept, and offers that aren't accepted in time are withdrawn and given to the next child on the waiting list. accepted offers go to the school office, which sends the welcome pack. parents who are refused can appeal to the independent panel, and if the panel upholds the appeal the school has to offer a place.

errors.detail: There is no catchment decision (e.g. 'Inside catchment?') after the home address check. Council Admissions/Home Address never connect to the School offer or to the waiting list, so the inside-catchment and everyone-else paths are missing.

The edge 'School -> Waiting List: offers place' is wrong. Children inside the catchment get the offer from the school, and only the others go on the waiting list. The duplicate 'routes to' edge between the same boxes is also unsupported.
'Offer withdrawn' dead-ends. The text says a withdrawn offer is given to the next child on the waiting list, so it should loop back to the Waiting List and then to a new offer.

When the appeal is upheld the school has to offer a place, but 'Offer Place' is a dead-end box with no link to the School. The 'Accepted in time?' decision is also fed from Parents, with no offer feeding into it.

description: a taxpayer files a return through the tax portal, which runs it through the validation engine. returns with errors are sent back to the taxpayer to fix, and the rest go to the risk scorer. low risk returns are paid automatically by the treasury system, anything above that waits for a case officer. the case officer asks the taxpayer for receipts and if they don't arrive within thirty days the officer rejects the refund. otherwise the officer approves it and the treasury system pays it.

errors.detail: The case officer's request for receipts goes to a 'Receipts' box instead of to the Taxpayer, so the taxpayer is never asked and the request/response exchange with them is lost.
The 'Overdue?' decision is checked by the 'Receipts' box, but it is the case officer who decides whether the receipts arrived within thirty days.
The 'Approved?' decision is not in the text. The text says that if the receipts arrive in time, the officer simply approves the refund. The decision's 'no' outcome also has no edge, so it dead-ends.

The officer's approval step is missing. 'Overdue?' no goes to the invented 'Approved?' decision rather than to an approval by the Case Officer that then leads to Treasury System paying. The rejection outcome ends at a generic 'Refund' box and does not clearly show the officer rejecting the refund.

description: the courier scans a parcel at the locker bank and the locker controller looks for a free compartment of the right size. if there isn't one the courier takes the parcel back to the depot, otherwise the controller opens the door and the courier drops the parcel in. the controller texts the recipient a pickup code. a recipient who doesn't collect within three days gets a reminder, and after five days the controller flags the parcel for return and the courier picks it up on the next round.

errors.detail: The 'yes' outcome of 'Compartment free?' points back to Locker Bank, but the text says the controller opens the door, so it should go to the Door step.
The 'no' outcome of 'Compartment free?' is missing; when no compartment is free the courier takes the parcel back to the Depot.
The courier's edges are swapped: 'takes back' goes to Door and 'drops in' goes to Depot, when the courier takes the parcel back to the Depot and drops it into the opened compartment.
The collection check hangs off Recipient, but the controller is the one that tracks non-collection and decides to send a reminder.

There is no five-day check for the return flag. Reminder leads straight to Return Flag, so the flag looks like it always follows the reminder. The text says the controller flags the parcel only when it is still uncollected after five days.

description: the shot firer loads the blast holes and wires them to the firing box. before every blast the site supervisor sweeps the exclusion zone and the blast only goes ahead when the zone is clear, if anyone is inside the supervisor sounds the siren and sweeps again. the shot firer fires the blast and waits fifteen minutes for fumes. then he inspects the face for misfires, and any misfired hole is reported to the mine manager who decides whether to refire it. after the all clear the loader moves in to dig the broken rock.

errors.detail: The 'Zone clear?' decision is fed by Firing Box, but the site supervisor's sweep of the exclusion zone is what determines whether the zone is clear.
The 'yes' outcome of 'Zone clear?' goes to Site Supervisor, but when the zone is clear the blast goes ahead and the shot firer fires it.
The Siren is a dead end. The text says that after the siren the supervisor sweeps again, so the flow should return to the sweep and the zone check.
There is no 'fire the blast' step by the shot firer. The Shot Firer goes straight to waiting for fumes without the blast being fired.
Fumes does not connect to Inspection, so the inspection of the face after the wait has no incoming flow and the process breaks there.
The 'no misfire' outcome of 'Misfire?' is missing. The all-clear path to the Loader moving in is absent, so the Loader has no incoming edge.
The edge Loader -> 'Dig Rock' uses a box that is not in the boxes list, so the digging step is not properly defined.
The mine manager's decision on whether to refire is drawn as a plain 'decides' edge to Refire rather than a yes/no decision, and a refire does not lead back into the blast or inspection flow.

description: the brewer mashes the grain and the wort goes to the kettle for the boil. the chiller cools the wort into the fermenter and the brewer pitches yeast. the lab takes a gravity reading every day and the beer moves to the conditioning tank only once the gravity stops dropping, until then it stays in the fermenter. from conditioning the beer is filtered and goes either to the canning line or the keg filler, depending on the order. any can that the fill checker finds underfilled is kicked off the line.

errors.detail: Nothing connects Kettle to Chiller, so the flow dead-ends at the kettle although the chiller cools the boiled wort.
The 'Underfilled?' decision is fed by Keg Filler, but the Fill Checker checks cans, so the check should come from the Fill Checker after the Canning Line.
The 'yes' outcome of 'Underfilled?' goes to Fill Checker, and no step shows the underfilled can being kicked off the line.
Yeast has no edge into the Fermenter, so the pitching step dead-ends.

description: a doping control officer collects a urine sample from the athlete and splits it into an a bottle and a b bottle. both bottles go to the accredited lab. the lab tests the a sample and negative results are reported to the federation and closed. if the a sample is positive the federation notifies the athlete, who can ask for the b sample to be tested. when the b sample confirms it the federation suspends the athlete, otherwise the case is dropped.

errors.detail: The 'Sample negative?' no branch (a positive result) goes to Closed, but a positive A sample should lead to the federation notifying the athlete.
After a negative result is reported to the Federation, nothing leads to Closed, so the negative path never closes the case.
'Sample positive?' is checked from Federation, but the lab's A-sample test determines whether the result is positive.
'Bottle confirmed?' is checked from Federation, not from the B sample test. The B Sample box dead-ends and the athlete's request never reaches the confirmation decision.
The 'Sample positive?' no outcome is not drawn. The 'Federation notifies athlete' step is also drawn as the decision's yes edge going to Athlete instead of as an edge from Federation.

description: a client sends a document to the translation agency's project manager, who gets a quote from the pricing tool. if the client accepts the quote the project manager assigns a translator, else the request is archived. the translator works in the cat tool, which checks every segment against the translation memory and fills in exact matches automatically. a proofreader checks the finished translation and sends anything with errors back to the translator. the project manager delivers the final file and the billing team invoices the client.

errors.detail: Nothing connects the translator or CAT tool to the Proofreader, so the proofreading step has no incoming flow and the finished translation never reaches it.
The edge Proofreader -> Translation Memory 'checks' is not in the text. The proofreader checks the finished translation, not the memory.

There is no decision for whether the proofreader finds errors, and no 'no errors' path passing the translation to the Project Manager. The send-back edge is unconditional and the proofreader dead-ends.
The Project Manager delivers the final file to the Billing Team, but the text says the file is delivered to the client.
The 'Quote accepted?' decision is fed by the Project Manager, but the client is the one who accepts or rejects the quote.
An extra 'Translation Agency' box sits between Client and Project Manager, with a bogus 'gets quote from' edge. The client should send the document directly to the Project Manager.

description: each elevator reports faults to the remote monitoring service. the service tries to reset the elevator remotely, and if the reset works it logs the fault and does nothing else. when the reset fails it raises a call with the maintenance dispatcher, who sends the nearest technician. if someone is trapped inside the dispatcher also calls the fire brigade. the technician repairs the elevator and the monitoring service watches it for an hour before closing the call.

errors.detail: The 'Logs Fault' box leads on to 'Maintenance Dispatcher' with 'raises call', but the text says a successful reset logs the fault and nothing else happens.
'Reset succeeded?' has no 'no' edge. When the reset fails the service should raise a call with the Maintenance Dispatcher.
'Nearest Technician' is a dead end, and the repair edge starts from a separate duplicate 'Technician' box. The technician the dispatcher sends should be the one who repairs the elevator.
The monitoring service is shown watching the Technician, but the text says it watches the elevator after the repair.
The final step is missing: after watching for an hour the monitoring service closes the call. No closing step or edge exists.

description: a skier books skis online and the rental system reserves a pair in their size at the shop. at the shop the technician adjusts the bindings to the skier's weight and the skier signs the waiver. skis come back at the end of the day through the return counter, where staff check them for damage. damaged skis go to the repair bench, the rest are waxed and put back on the rack. if the repair bench can't fix them the shop manager writes them off.

errors.detail: The 'Damaged Skis?' decision has no incoming edge. Staff check the skis for damage, but Staff is a dead end and never connects to the decision, so the damaged/rest branching is detached from the flow.
The edge 'Online Rental' → 'Return Counter' ('sends back') is not in the text. The skis come back through the return counter, not from the online rental system.

The edge 'Repair Bench' → 'Rack' is not described. The text sends only the undamaged ('the rest') skis to be waxed and racked, and the repair bench's only stated outcome is a write-off when it can't fix them.
The repair outcome should be a decision box such as 'Can repair fix?'. Instead, the condition 'can't fix' is used as an edge label, and there is no yes/no branch for the repair outcome.
The Technician is shown signing the waiver ('Technician' → 'Waiver'). The text says the skier signs it, so the edge should come from Skier.

description: farmers send seed samples to the seed bank, where a technician cleans and counts them. the technician runs a germination test, and samples that germinate below eighty five percent are sent back to the farmer for a fresh sample. good samples are dried to five percent moisture and sealed in foil bags. the bags go to the minus twenty vault. every ten years the curator retests a portion of each sample, and if germination has dropped the curator asks the regeneration field to grow fresh seed.

errors.detail: The decision 'Germinated below 85%?' has no 'no' edge, so good samples never go on to be dried; the only route to 'Dried Sample' is through 'Fresh Sample'.
The edge 'Fresh Sample' -> 'Dried Sample' is not in the text. Failed samples are sent back to the farmer and are not dried and sealed.

There is no decision box for 'germination has dropped?'. 'Retest' goes straight to 'Growth Field', so regeneration is requested after every retest, not only when germination has dropped, and the path where it hasn't dropped is missing.
The ten-year retest interval is not captured.

description: sewage arrives at the treatment works and passes through the screens, which remove rags into a skip. the grit channel settles out sand and the flow goes on to the primary tanks. the aeration lanes treat the water next, and there are four lanes using round robin. a turbidity sensor sits in front of the river outfall and diverts any cloudy water back to the aeration lanes. sludge from the primary tanks is pumped to the digester, which makes biogas for the generator.

errors.detail: There is no edge from Screens to Grit Channel, so the flow dead-ends after the screens and the grit channel is unreachable.
The edge 'Aeration Lanes → Sewage' is backwards and wrong. Water should flow from Primary Tanks to Aeration Lanes, and that edge is missing.
Treated water never goes from Aeration Lanes to the Turbidity Sensor, which sits in front of the River Outfall and should take over the outfall's incoming flow.

The send-back of cloudy water starts at River Outfall, but it should start at the Turbidity Sensor via a 'Cloudy water?' decision. The yes branch goes back to Aeration Lanes and the no branch goes to River Outfall. The sensor-to-outfall edge is mislabeled as a diversion instead of 'routes to'.

description: a steward finds a lost item and hands it to the lost and found desk. the desk logs it in the property system and anything valuable goes into the safe. when a fan reports a lost item online the property system searches for a match. on a match the desk emails the fan to collect it, and on a miss the system keeps the report open for thirty days. unclaimed items are given to charity after ninety days, except phones, which the desk wipes and recycles.

errors.detail: The steward hands the item to a separate 'Lost and Found' box that has no outgoing edges, so the steward is never connected to the 'Desk' that logs the item.
The edge 'Property System → Fan: searches for' and 'Fan → Online Match' are reversed or garbled. The fan should report the lost item to the property system, which then searches for a match.
'Match?' is checked by the Desk, but the text says the property system searches for the match.
The 'yes' outcome of the match goes from Property System to 'Keep Open' (the miss path). A match should lead to the desk emailing the fan, and 'Match?' has no 'yes' edge.
The desk emailing the fan to collect the item on a match is absent.
'Charity → Phone?' puts the phone check after the charity donation. Phones are the exception to the donation, so 'Unclaimed?' should lead to 'Phone?', with 'no' going to Charity.
The 'Phone?' 'no' path to Charity is missing, and the wiped phone is never recycled, so the flow dead-ends at 'Wipe'.

description: a family fills in an adoption form at the shelter and the adoption counsellor reviews it. families with a garden and no other dogs move straight to a meet and greet, the rest get a home visit first. if the home visit fails the counsellor declines the application. at the meet and greet the behaviourist watches the dog with the family, and only if the behaviourist is happy does the family pay the fee. the vet microchips the dog before it goes home.

errors.detail: The 'Garden dog?' decision is checked from Family, but the adoption counsellor reviews the form and sends families to a meet and greet or a home visit.
'Home visit failed?' has no 'no' edge, so a family that passes the home visit never continues to the meet and greet.

The decision after the behaviourist should be whether they are happy, and its 'yes' outcome should be the family paying the fee. There is no pay-fee step and no behaviourist-happy question, and 'Fee paid?' does not match the text.
'Fee paid?' yes loops back to Family, and Family then goes to Vet through an ungated edge, so the microchipping is not sequenced after the behaviourist approval and fee payment.
The final step of the dog going home after microchipping is not shown.

description: an advertiser books a radio spot through the sales rep, who checks the traffic system for free slots. if the slot is taken the rep offers the next free slot, and the advertiser either takes it or cancels. the creative team records the ad and legal reviews the script. ads that make health claims need sign off from the compliance manager. the traffic system then schedules the ad into the playout system, which plays it and sends a proof of play to billing.

errors.detail: The 'no' outcome of 'Slot taken?' goes to 'Take it?', but when the slot is free the booking should simply proceed, because no alternative slot is offered.
'Take it?' has no outgoing edges: the 'yes' path (booking accepted, moving on) and the 'no' path (advertiser cancels) are both absent.

There is no health-claims decision box. 'Creative Team' links straight to 'Compliance Manager', so sign off looks unconditional and skips legal review. The non-health path (legal review straight to scheduling) is also missing.

The creative, legal and compliance branch is not connected to the booking flow, and its approval does not feed into 'Traffic System' scheduling the ad. 'Legal Review' and 'Compliance Manager' dead-end, and 'Traffic System' schedules without waiting for them.
The playout step is incomplete. The ad plays, and the proof of play goes to billing only after that, but 'Playout System' sends proof to 'Billing' with no playing step in between.
The edge 'Next Free Slot' to 'Take it?' is labeled 'yes', which makes it look like a decision outcome. It is a plain offer step and should have a neutral label.

description: the archivist pulls a box of letters and the conservator checks each letter's condition. fragile letters go to the conservation studio to be repaired first, the others go straight to the scanning room. the scanner operator scans each letter and the ocr service extracts the text. pages where the ocr confidence is low go to volunteers to transcribe by hand. the catalogue publishes the scans with the text and the archivist returns the box to the stacks.

errors.detail: There is no 'Fragile?' decision box after the conservator's check. The conservator sends every letter both to the studio and to the scanning room, with no yes/no split.
Conservation Studio points back to Archivist, but repaired letters should go on to the Scanning Room.
The 'Low confidence?' decision has no 'no' path. Pages with good OCR confidence should go on to the Catalogue for publishing.
Volunteers and Hand Transcription dead-end. The hand-transcribed text should flow on to the Catalogue for publishing.
Catalogue has no incoming edges, so the OCR output and the scans never reach publishing. Archivist returns the box to the stacks directly rather than after publishing.
The separate 'Hand Transcription' and 'Text' boxes are extra. 'Catalogue → Text' is a questionable edge, because the catalogue publishes the scans together with the text.

description: green beans arrive from the importer and the quality lab roasts a small sample. if the sample cups below eighty points the roastery returns the lot to the importer. accepted lots go to the warehouse until the head roaster schedules them. the roaster drops each batch into the cooling tray and the colour meter reads it, and batches outside the target colour are sold as seconds. good batches rest for two days, then the packing machine bags them and the web shop ships orders.

errors.detail: The 'Sample under 80?' decision has no 'no' edge, so accepted lots never go to the Warehouse and the Warehouse has no incoming flow.
Seconds -> Packing Machine ('rest for') is invented. Batches sold as seconds are not rested or packed, and this edge sends the out-of-colour path into packing.
The 'Out of colour?' decision has no 'no' outcome. Good batches should rest for two days and then go to the Packing Machine, but this path is missing and the resting step is not a box.

The edge 'Quality Lab -> Importer' (roasts sample) points at the Importer. The green beans should flow to the Quality Lab, which roasts the sample, so the lot never reaches the lab and the Importer-to-beans direction is also reversed.

description: a drone flies along the bridge and photographs every girder. the photos go to a crack detection model, which flags any crack longer than five millimetres. the bridge engineer reviews the flagged photos and sends a rope access team for anything she can't judge from the photo. if the team or the engineer finds a serious crack the engineer closes a lane and orders a repair, otherwise the crack is added to the watch list. the drone rechecks watch list cracks every three months.

errors.detail: The 'Clear from Photo?' decision sends 'yes' to Rope Team, but the rope team is sent for cracks the engineer can't judge from the photo, so the polarity is inverted and the rope team is on the wrong branch.
Rope Team has no outgoing edge. The text says the team's findings feed the serious-crack decision, so the flow dead-ends there.

The path where the engineer can judge the photo herself is absent. Bridge Engineer goes to 'Serious crack?' directly and in parallel with the photo-check decision, so the serious-crack decision is not made after the rope team or the engineer's own judgement.
The photos go from the Drone to the Crack Detection Model, but the diagram draws the edge from Bridge to the model.
The engineer orders the repair, but the diagram shows Lane ordering Repair. Repair should hang off the engineer or the serious-crack decision, alongside closing the lane.

description: the launch director polls each console for a go. propulsion, range safety and weather all report to the director. if any console says no go the director holds the count, fixes the issue and polls again. on a full go the ground computer runs the terminal count. the flight computer takes over at ten seconds and aborts the launch on any sensor fault, otherwise it ignites the engines and releases the clamps.

errors.detail: Propulsion, Range Safety and Weather are chained to each other (Propulsion→Range Safety→Weather→Director) and are not connected to the polled consoles. The text says each of them reports directly to the director.
The 'Console failed?' decision has no 'no' (full go) outcome to the Ground Computer. The Ground Computer has no incoming edge, so the flow never reaches the terminal count.
The step where the director holds the count and fixes the issue before polling again is missing. The 'yes' edge goes straight back to the Launch Director.
There is no handoff from the terminal count (Ground Computer) to the Flight Computer taking over at ten seconds. Terminal Count is a dead end and the Flight Computer is unreachable.
On a sensor fault the diagram goes to Clamps, but the text says the launch is aborted. There is no abort box.
The 'no' (no fault) branch goes only to Engines. The engines should be ignited and then the clamps released, but Clamps is wired to the fault 'yes' branch instead of following Engines.

The direct Flight Computer→Clamps ('ignites') and Flight Computer→Engines edges bypass the sensor-fault decision. They make ignition unconditional and wrongly show the Flight Computer igniting the clamps.

description: teams submit their projects on the hackathon site, which checks the submission has a demo video. submissions without a video are marked incomplete and the site emails the team, who can resubmit until the deadline. complete submissions are split across judges using round robin. each judge scores the project and projects with a big score gap between judges go to the head judge to break the tie. the organisers announce the top three from the final scores.

errors.detail: The 'Demo video?' yes path to the judges is missing. Its only outgoing edge goes to 'Yes', which is not a box, and the 'no' outcome is not drawn at all.
'Submissions incomplete?' has no incoming edge. The incomplete-marking should follow from the 'Demo video?' check failing, so that check never leads to the email step.

After the email, the team's resubmission should loop back to the Hackathon Site to be checked again. Instead it goes through a nonexistent 'Resubmit until deadline' box straight to the judges, which skips the video check.
The 'Score gap?' no outcome is missing. Projects without a big gap should go straight to the organisers for the final scores and top-three announcement.

description: the manufacturer ships vaccine boxes with a temperature logger to the national store. the store manager reads the logger on arrival and quarantines any box that went above eight degrees, the rest go into the walk in fridge. district nurses order vaccines from the store every week and the store packs them in cool boxes with ice packs. at the clinic the nurse checks the vial monitor and only uses vials whose monitor hasn't changed colour. used vials are counted and the count goes back to the store manager for restocking.

errors.detail: There is no 'above eight degrees?' decision box. The Store Manager connects straight to both Quarantine Box and Walk In Fridge, so the yes/no split between quarantined boxes and 'the rest' is lost.
The Cool Box is a dead end. The text says the store packs vaccines for the district nurses, and the nurse then uses them at the clinic, but nothing links the Cool Box to the Nurse or clinic.
The 'Color stable?' decision is checked from Vial Monitor. The text says the nurse makes this decision after checking the monitor.
The 'yes' outcome of 'Color stable?' loops back to Vial Monitor. The text says such vials are used, so it should lead to a 'use vials' step.
There is no 'use vials' step. The vials with an unchanged monitor are never used, and the 'used vials' that are counted never appear.
Vial Count is fed directly by Vial Monitor ('counts'). The text says used vials are counted, so the count should come from the used vials, not from the monitor.
The 'no' outcome of 'Color stable?' (vials whose monitor changed colour are not used) is missing.
The edge from Temperature Logger to Store Manager is labelled 'routes to'. The text says the store manager reads the logger, so the relation is the wrong way round and wrongly labelled.
The ice packs used when packing the cool boxes are not shown, and the weekly ordering is not captured.
